reports.title: Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Interim Financial Statements(In US dollars) HUDBAY MINERALS INC. For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025

lines: • Further improved full year 2026 consolidated cash cost1 guidance range to $(0.55) to $(0.35) per pound of copper, an additional improvement from the previously updated guidance range of $(0.45) to $(0.25) per pound of copper, as year-to-date results are trending well below the low end of the cash cost range.

• Improved full year 2026 consolidated sustaining cash cost guidance range to $1.40 to $1.80 per pound copper from the original guidance range of $1.70 to $2.10 per pound of copper as a result of strong exposure to gold by-product credits and continued strong operating cost control.

Full year 2026 consolidated sustaining capital expenditures expected to be $35 million lower than guidance levels due to lower capitalized stripping in Peru and British Columbia and capital deferrals and efficiencies.

Peru cash cost1, net of by-product credits, of $2.23 per pound exceeded the upper end of the 2026 annual guidance range of $1.70 to $2.10 per pound primarily due to lower by-product credits, partially offset by better treatment and refining charges.
Manitoba cash cost1 of $403 per ounce of gold outperformed the low end of the 2026 annual guidance range of $500 to $800 per ounce as a result of higher by-product prices.

With the successful execution of its disciplined capital allocation strategy, attracting Mitsubishi as a long-term strategic joint venture partner and a prudent project funding plan, Hudbay's Copper World capital contributions are expected to be approximately $500 million, representing less than 25% of the initial growth capital, with capital contributions not expected to be required until 2028.

desk.headline: Record revenue more than doubles to $765.9m, beat; EPS $0.34 a cent short; 2026 cost guidance cut again, production reaffirmed

numbers.eps_basis: basic and diluted IFRS (adjusted EPS also $0.34)

results: Revenue rose 121% to a record $765.9m, helped by higher copper and gold output and prices; gold sales alone were $259.2m.
Net profit for shareholders fell to $149.5m ($0.34 a share) from $222.4m, but last year's quarter included a $322.3m pre-tax impairment reversal.
Cash cost after by-product credits was negative at $(0.19) per pound of copper, as gold credits more than covered operating costs.
Peru costs of $2.23/lb ran above the annual range, while Manitoba gold costs of $403/oz came in well below its range.
Net debt is about nil; credit lines were raised to $700m, and a C$0.01 quarterly dividend was declared.

guidance.summary: Hudbay cut its 2026 cost guidance for the second time, which is an improvement, and kept its copper and gold production ranges. Sustaining capital spending should come in about $35m below plan, while 2026 Copper World spending rises to $245m after the go-ahead.

points: Hudbay and Mitsubishi approved building Copper World, a roughly $2bn first phase aiming for first copper in the second half of 2029.
Hudbay's own share of the build is about $500m from 2028, with partner cash, a Wheaton stream and project debt covering the rest.
Management expects group copper output to rise about 25% in 2027, with gold roughly flat.
Constancia in Peru ran at record throughput; Copper Mountain's mill rate and a court challenge in British Columbia are the main watch points.
With net cash and a bigger credit line, more shareholder returns will be weighed as cash flow allows.
call.source: Press release (Exhibit 99.3) and call coverage: Motley Fool transcript, 13 Nov 2026; Investing.com, 12 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Peru costs come back inside the annual range in Q4.
Copper World construction start and the Q1 2027 hearing on the British Columbia court challenge.
2027 production and cost guidance, expected with full-year results.
